source.source_title: iPod touch (5th generation) - Technical Specifications - Apple Support (IE)
source.verification_notes: Official Apple technical-specification page captured as original HTML on 2026-11-11; 18 technical sections extracted. The first record section preserves model-identification evidence from Apple's separate identification page.
notes: Technical specifications in the following sections are transcribed from the model-specific Apple technical-specification page; each section carries its own source URL and archive path.

The first section preserves model number/introduction-date evidence from Apple's separate identification page: https://support.apple.com/en-ie/103823, archived at apple_remaining_extraction/technical_specs_html/ipod-index.html.

extraction.note: Official Apple iPod identification text retained. Explicit model numbers, introduction dates, capacity options and navigation interface extracted where present with source-section provenance. These are identification-page records, not full historical technical-specification sheets; no absent specs inferred.

sections.heading: iPod touch and the Environment
sections.source_text:
Apple takes a complete product life cycle approach to determining our environmental impact. Learn more
iPod touch embodies Apple’s continuing environmental progress. It is designed with the following features to reduce environmental impact:
Mercury-free LED-backlit display
Arsenic-free display glass
Brominated flame retardant-free
PVC-free
Recyclable aluminum enclosure
Apple and the Environment
Learn more about Apple’s dedication to reducing the environmental impact of our products and process. Apple Product Environmental Reports detail the environmental attributes of our products.
Recycling
Apple takes a holistic view of materials management and waste minimization. Learn more about how to recycle your iPod touch.
Weight varies by configuration and manufacturing process.
1GB = 1 billion bytes; actual formatted capacity less.
Internet access required; broadband recommended; fees may apply.
For iPod touch with Maps, the Maps application provides your approximate location using information based on your proximity to known Wi-Fi networks (when on and available). The more accurate the available information, the smaller the circle identifying your position on the map. The feature is not available in all areas. Known Wi-Fi networks are predominantly in urban areas. In order to provide your location, data is collected in a form that does not personally identify you. If you do not want such data collected, do not enable the feature. Not enabling the feature will not impact the functionality of your iPod touch.
Testing conducted by Apple in August 2012 using preproduction iPod touch hardware and software. The playlist contained 358 unique audio tracks consisting of content imported from CDs using iTunes (128-Kbps AAC) and content purchased from the iTunes Store (256-Kbps AAC); video content was purchased from the iTunes Store. iPod units were associated to a Wi-Fi network; all other settings were default. Battery tests are conducted with specific iPod units; actual results may vary. Rechargeable batteries have a limited number of charge cycles and may eventually need to be replaced ( www.apple.com/uk/support/ipod/service/battery ). Battery life and number of charge cycles vary by use and settings. See www.apple.com/uk/batteries for more information.
iPod and iTunes are for legal or rightholder-authorized copying only. Don’t steal music.
Some features may not be available for all countries or all areas. Click here to see complete list.
